newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends down as selling continues.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends down as selling continues.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended sharply weaker on Tuesday as long liquidation and origin selling continued to eat into prices against a background of shallow demand.
Traders said disappointment over the market's failure to sustain its recent rally and talk that the Ivorian crop could overtake initial expectations was playing into sellers hands.
"It was a four-week uptrend and it's (almost) gone in two days," said one trader.
"Crop ideas have gone up and there was no follow-up after that magical 999 stg on December."
The most active March contract shed 13 stg at the close to stand at a session low of 998 stg while front-month December was just above lows at 973 stg, also a decline of 13 stg.
Turnover on the day totalled a modest 4,344 lots.
The market is likely to adopt a wait-and-see approach to Ivorian arrivals which start on October 15 while forecasts on the size of the crop still occupy a wide range.
But some traders remained sceptical about the significance of early arrivals.
"It should be interesting. But just a few weeks are not going to tell you anything," said one trader.
But any delay, which according to some forecasters seems to be an unlikely scenario, is set to prop up the Dec/March spread which has been under pressure recently.
On the switches, Dec/March moved from 27 stg to 28 stg briefly, before settling back at 26 stg. March/Sept traded at 31 stg while March/March saw no deals.
